ground_truth.title: Ultimate Backpacking Checklist & Gear Essentials
ground_truth.author: Heather Eldridge
ground_truth.main_content:
We’ve spent decades honing our backpacking gear to (our) perfect balance of weight and creature comforts. After 20,000 miles and 1,000 nights on trail, we’re pretty dialed in to what we want and need for any adventure, and we love helping people find their perfect kit as well.

We’ve organized the Ultimate Backpacking Checklist into categories to make it easier for you to gather your backpacking gear for your next trip. We also have a downloadable checklist. Print it out and have a hard copy with you as you organize your gear.

Ultimate Backpacking Checklist

*We consider items in italics to be optional

SHELTER

Tent

Rainfly

Tent poles or trekking poles

Stakes

Guylines

Groundsheet for tent floor durability

BACKPACK & STORAGE

Backpack

Trash compactor bag or waterproof stuff sacks for interior rain protection

Large Ziploc for garbage

Shoulder strap camera pocket

Summit pack

ENTERTAINMENT

Book or Kindle

Crossword puzzles

Cribbage or dice

Notebook + pen

Headphones

NAVIGATION EQUIPMENT

Always be prepared and know how to use your map and compass, even if you plan to use a GPS or GPS app.

Topo map(s)

Waterproof map bag / Ziploc

Compass

Watch

GPS or GPS phone app with maps downloaded for offline use

Satellite Messenger/PLB for remote locations

Download driving directions for offline use

Photos of guidebook pages

Check current weather before trip

Call ranger station pre-trip for trail conditions + regulations

2 copies of itinerary: 1 left with friend + 1 under car seat

Backpacking permits

FIRST AID

Band-aids of various sizes

Antibiotic ointment

Gauze pads

Medical tape

Latex gloves

Tweezers

Safety pins

Moleskin

Antihistamines

Antidiarrheal

Check out our Best First Aid Kits list for more suggestions

PERSONAL TOILETRIES

Sunscreen + lip balm

Bug repellant

Toiletries (biodegradable shampoo, etc.)

Prescription Rx

OTC meds + vitamins

Contact lenses + supplies/glasses

Toilet paper/wipes + sealable bag to pack it out

Digging trowel

Menstrual products

Hand sanitizer

Toothbrush, paste + floss

Comb/brush

Earplugs + eye mask

Eye drops

Hair ties

Nail clipper

Pre-trip: Clip nails, cut hair, shave, etc.

COOKING & KITCHEN

Stove

Pot

Fuel

Lighter

Coffee maker

FOOD

Provisions – commonly between 2,500-3,500 calories per day

Extra day’s supply of food for emergencies

Food bag / Ursack

50’ nylon cord + small carabiner for bear bag hanging or bear canister where required

OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT FOR SNOWY & ICY TRIPS

Ice axe – learn + practice proper self-arrest technique

Traction devices

SLEEP SYSTEM

Sleeping bag / backpacking quilt

Pad attachment straps (optional)

Sleeping pad

Pump sack (optional)

Pillow

TOOLS & ACCESSORIES

Trekking poles

Lightweight hammock

Backpacking chair / sit pad

Light pocket knife or multitool

Phone (turn on low power/airplane mode)

Waterproof phone case

Umbrella

Bear spray for grizzly country

Camera + waterproof case/Ziploc

Extra camera battery

Headlamp (check batteries pre-trip)

Extra batteries for long trips

Power bank + charging cords

Wall plug for thru-hikes

Assorted Ziploc bags

Cash, ID, credit card, insurance card

EMERGENCY KIT

Whistle

Duct / Tenacious Tape for repairs

Sleeping pad patch kit

Super glue

Needle + thread

Small Sharpie

Stormproof matches + small fire starters

Small backup lighter

Backup water treatment pills (Chlorine Dioxide)

HYDRATION

2-4 water bottles (ability to carry 2-6 liters depending on climate) or a hydration pack & bladder

Collapsible water containers for carrying lots of water in dry locations

Water treatment

Pre-filter for water treatment, ex: pantyhose

CLOTHING

All clothing items should be lightweight, moisture-wicking and quick-drying (synthetic or wool, no cotton).

Hiking pants ( Men’s / Women’s ) & shorts ( Men’s / Women’s )

Wicking shirt/tank & long-sleeve sun shirt ( Men’s / Women’s )

1-2 pairs quick-dry underwear

Down jacket and/or fleece jacket

Rain jacket

Rain pants for wet trips

Windbreaker depending on forecast

Base layers

Shoes

2-4 Pair socks

PACK IN CAR

Parking pass for car

Clean clothes + shoes to change into

Gallon of water for trailhead shower

Camp towel to dry off

Water + snacks

Backpacking Tips

LIGHTEN YOUR LOAD – Start by weeding out things you don’t need. Be careful with every choice you make, a few ounces here and there can add a lot of weight in the end. A lightweight backpacking checklist, like the one here, will help you to focus on essential items. Next, focus on lightening your heaviest gear: shelter, backpack, and sleeping bag. Switching your traditional big three out for lightweight options is the best opportunity for weight savings, especially when you’re starting out. If you invest in a lightweight shelter, backpack, and sleeping bag, you can easily cut 10 or more pounds and be well on your way to having an ultralight backpacking setup.

CLOTHING FOR BACKPACKING – The clothing you pack will change slightly depending on the conditions you expect to encounter on specific trips, but the fundamentals remain the same. Clothing made with quick-drying fabrics that wick moisture away from your skin are best to help your body thermoregulate and stay comfortable in both hot and cold environments. Nylon, polyester, wool, bamboo, silk, and synthetic blends are all good options. Avoid cotton – it absorbs moisture and takes a long time to dry, which can cause a variety of problems including blisters and chafing. Choose items that can be worn together in layers. Fleece and goose-down have the best warmth-to-weight ratio and make the best insulation materials for backpackers. Rain gear should be lightweight, breathable, and waterproof.

BACKPACKING FOOD – Good food is really important for any backpacking trip, so it’s well worth the effort to put together a simple meal plan before your trip. Keeping food weight down is a critical backpacking skill that usually takes experience to master. A good place to start is our Guide to Lightweight Backpacking Food. Most seasoned backpackers opt for lightweight, calorically-dense foods that are very easy to prepare. Packaged freeze-dried meals and snack foods can be great, but keep in mind, they tend to be very high in sodium/sugar, which can take their toll, if eaten in excess.

Another approach is to prepare your own backpacking meals, using a food dehydrator to dry meats, fruits, veggies, and sauces. Combining them with spices and quick-cooking or easily rehydrated dried goods such as pasta, couscous, instant potatoes, instant refried beans, and minute rice is a great way to customize your own highly-nutritious meals. This method takes more time and effort, and you must be more willing to carry more weight, but making your meals can be more cost-effective and healthier for long trips. Our approach is usually a mix of both methods. For more specifics about food, check out our Best Lightweight Backpacking Food guide, where we outline our general backpacking food strategy and suggest some of our favorite meals.

CleverHiker Backpacking Video Series

If you’re new to backpacking, or have been hiking with outdated equipment, we highly recommend watching our two professionally-filmed video series (below), where we’ll teach you everything you need to know to start backpacking -the skills and the gear.

Essential Trail Skills – 20 HD tutorial videos to teach the most critical skills for backpackers of all levels, such as: Leave No Trace, Backpacking Trip Planning, How to Find and Fit the Right Backpack, How to Pack a Lightweight Backpack, and much more.

Lightweight Backpacking Basics – One of the main reasons to minimize your pack weight is to maximum your freedom on the trail. Backpacking with a lighter pack will reduce stress on your body, give you more free time on the trail, and allow you to hike farther with less effort. In this 10-episode series, you’ll learn all about the gear that will allow you to hike lighter to make the hiking the most enjoyable part of your trip.

ground_truth.main_content_markdown:
We’ve spent decades honing our backpacking gear to (our) perfect balance of weight and creature comforts. After 20,000 miles and 1,000 nights on trail, we’re pretty dialed in to what we want and need for any adventure, and we love helping people find their perfect kit as well.

We’ve organized the Ultimate Backpacking Checklist into categories to make it easier for you to gather your backpacking gear for your next trip. We also have a downloadable checklist. Print it out and have a hard copy with you as you organize your gear.

## Ultimate Backpacking Checklist

*We consider items in italics to be optional

### SHELTER

- [Tent](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-tents-backpacking/)

- Rainfly

- Tent poles or [trekking poles](https://www.cleverhiker.com/hiking/best-hiking-trekking-poles/)

- [Stakes](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-tent-stakes/)

- [Guylines](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-tent-stakes/)

- [Groundsheet](https://www.amazon.com/Tyvek-House-Wrap-Ground-Sheet/dp/B074FSQ1H2/ref=as_li_ss_tl?ref_=fsclp_pl_dp_1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=40bd77982223c98e8ee86a5e98e5c4a0&language=en_US) for tent floor durability

### BACKPACK & STORAGE

- [Backpack](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-backpacks/)

- [Trash compactor bag](https://www.amazon.com/Hefty-Strong-Multipurpose-Unscented-Drawstring/dp/B00HNW8CXA/ref=as_li_ss_tl?keywords=hefty+strong+trash+compactor+bags&qid=1561580290&s=gateway&sr=8-9-spons&psc=1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=8bd2470c3a3ce278bbd86dad9b8e53bd&language=en_US) or [waterproof stuff sacks](https://www.amazon.com/Sea-Summit-eVAC-Dry-Sack/dp/B001Q3KKPA/ref=as_li_ss_tl?th=1&psc=1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=b7664fd5be9aea1e5f170504cf2fe2e4) for interior rain protection

- [Large Ziploc](https://www.amazon.com/Ziploc-Freezer-Bags-Gallon-Count/dp/B00CQAHOCO/ref=as_li_ss_tl?keywords=freezer+ziploc&qid=1561580416&s=gateway&sr=8-5&th=1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=68528f8276e5f637bdc922ee6de18966&language=en_US) for garbage

- [Shoulder strap camera pocket](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=47cd1998-e608-4548-aa0f-3d33e964ad3a&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.hyperlitemountaingear.com/products/shoulder-pocket&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- Summit pack

### ENTERTAINMENT

- Book or [Kindle](https://www.amazon.com/All-New-Kindle-Paperwhite-High-Resolution-Display/dp/B00OQVZDJM/ref=as_li_ss_tl?ie=UTF8&qid=1448712060&sr=8-1&keywords=kindle+paperwhite&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=436744ecf1dea0098c1ba31eb9a4515c&language=en_US)

- Crossword puzzles

- Cribbage or [dice](https://www.amazon.com/Farkle-Keychain-Classic-Dice-Rolling-Risk-Taking/dp/B002BUYEGS?crid=1EPIXS05CGE8X&keywords=keychain+farkle&qid=1651271707&sprefix=keychain+farkle,aps,146&sr=8-1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=533b0a01c98c5127fd1a6f2bd2b643de&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)

- [Notebook](https://www.amazon.com/Rite-Rain-Weatherproof-Top-Spiral-946-3/dp/B01MQFDNSH/ref=as_li_ss_tl?keywords=rite+in+the+rain&qid=1561679913&s=gateway&sr=8-1&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=8083c7c2592255d91ba6050de72b69bd&language=en_US) + pen

- [Headphones](https://www.amazon.com/AfterShokz-Conduction-Wireless-Bluetooth-Headphones/dp/B07RQLTFJ5?crid=19FYJKRVR33GP&keywords=aftershokz+headphones&qid=1643270450&sprefix=after,aps,187&sr=8-3&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=2f1f54ba507f0afa74d3832ee3e1e1c0&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)

### NAVIGATION EQUIPMENT

Always be prepared and know how to use your map and compass, even if you plan to use a GPS or GPS app.

- Topo map(s)

- [Waterproof map bag](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&mi=10248&pw=180150&ctc=aae&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.rei.com%2Fproduct%2F211003%2Fsealline-map-case-medium) / Ziploc

- [Compass](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/890930/suunto-m-3-d-leader-compass%3Fcm_mmc%3Daff_AL-_-145262-_-180150-_-NA%26avad%3D180150_a15fb19b5&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- [Watch](https://www.cleverhiker.com/more-gear/best-gps-watches/)

- [GPS or GPS phone app](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/how-to-use-your-phone-as-a-gps-device-for-backpacking/) with maps downloaded for offline use

- [Satellite Messenger/PLB](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/c/plbs-and-satellite-messengers&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist) for remote locations

- Download driving directions for offline use

- Photos of guidebook pages

- [Check current weather](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/backcountry-weather-forecasts/) before trip

- Call ranger station pre-trip for trail conditions + regulations

- [2 copies of itinerary: 1 left with friend + 1 under car seat](https://www.cleverhiker.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/CleverHiker-Backpacking-Itinerary.pdf)

- Backpacking permits

### FIRST AID

- Band-aids of various sizes

- Antibiotic ointment

- Gauze pads

- Medical tape

- Latex gloves

- Tweezers

- Safety pins

- [Moleskin](https://www.amazon.com/Dr-Scholls-Moleskin-Plus-Each/dp/B00E4MK6AE/ref=as_li_ss_tl?keywords=moleskin&qid=1559081552&s=gateway&sr=8-5&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=5bd71f6cd9d799c9148aae4a9c71e829&language=en_US)

- Antihistamines

- Antidiarrheal

- Check out our [Best First Aid Kits](https://www.cleverhiker.com/more-gear/best-first-aid-kits/) list for more suggestions

### PERSONAL TOILETRIES

- [Sunscreen](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/207815/thinksport-everyday-face-naturally-tinted-spf-30-sunscreen-2-oz&ctc=Alvord%20Camping) + [lip balm](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/162355/sun-bum-mineral-spf-30-sunscreen-lip-balm&ctc=Alvord%20Camping)

- [Bug repellant](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/133911/sawyer-picaridin-insect-repellent-lotion-package-of-7&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- Toiletries (biodegradable shampoo, etc.)

- Prescription Rx

- OTC meds + vitamins

- Contact lenses + supplies/glasses

- Toilet paper/wipes + sealable bag to pack it out

- [Digging trowel](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/845328/rei-co-op-snow-stake%3Fcm_mmc%3Daff_AL-_-145262-_-180150-_-NA%26avad%3D180150_d15fd1b11&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- [Menstrual products](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/c/womens-hygiene-products&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- [Hand sanitizer](https://www.amazon.com/Advanced-Sanitizer-Portable-included-Carriers/dp/B01BOWFQTW/ref=as_li_ss_tl?keywords=small+hand+sanitizer&qid=1558388319&s=gateway&sr=8-3&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=ca1924efb97c8479f498197a68c5536a&language=en_US)

- Toothbrush, paste + floss

- Comb/brush

- Earplugs + eye mask

- Eye drops

- Hair ties

- Nail clipper

- Pre-trip: Clip nails, cut hair, shave, etc.

### COOKING & KITCHEN

- [Stove](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-stoves/)

- [Pot](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-cookware/)

- [Fuel](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&mi=10248&pw=180150&ctc=&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.rei.com%2Fproduct%2F849634%2Fmsr-isopro-fuel-canister-39-oz-110g)

- [Lighter](https://www.amazon.com/BIC-Lighter-3-Pack-Assorted-Colors/dp/B000Q0TNF2?tag=cleve05e-20)

- [Coffee maker](https://www.cleverhiker.com/camping/best-coffee-makers/)

### FOOD

- [Provisions](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-food-homepage/) – commonly between 2,500-3,500 calories per day

- Extra day’s supply of food for emergencies

- Food bag / [Ursack](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/124165/ursack-allmitey-bear-bag&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist)

- 50’ nylon cord + small carabiner for bear bag hanging or [bear canister](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/768902/bearvault-bv500-food-container&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist) where required

### OPTIONAL EQUIPMENT FOR SNOWY & ICY TRIPS

- [Ice axe](https://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&mi=10248&pw=180150&ctc=&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.rei.com%2Fproduct%2F177135%2Fcamp-corsa-ice-axe) – learn + practice [proper self-arrest technique](https://www.cleverhiker.com/tutorials/essential-trail-skills-video-series/crossing-snow-ice-axe-self-arrest-ep-16/)

- [Traction devices](https://www.cleverhiker.com/footwear/best-winter-traction-devices-crampons/)

### SLEEP SYSTEM

- [Sleeping bag](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-sleeping-bags/) / [backpacking quilt](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-quilts/)

- Pad attachment straps (optional)

- [Sleeping pad](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-sleeping-pads/)

- Pump sack (optional)

- [Pillow](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-hiking-camping-pillows/)

### TOOLS & ACCESSORIES

- [Trekking poles](https://www.cleverhiker.com/hiking/best-hiking-trekking-poles/)

- [Lightweight hammock](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-hammocks/)

- [Backpacking chair / sit pad](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-backpacking-chairs/)

- [Light pocket knife](https://www.cleverhiker.com/more-gear/best-pocket-knives/) or [multitool](https://www.cleverhiker.com/more-gear/best-multitools/)

- Phone (turn on low power/airplane mode)

- [Waterproof phone case](https://www.amazon.com/s/ref=as_li_ss_tl?k=lifeproof+phone+cases&ref=nb_sb_noss_2&linkCode=sl2&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=35e7c29b63cc7cf4eaee4d942177fd70&language=en_US)

- [Umbrella](https://www.amazon.com/Six-Moon-Designs-Silver-Ultralight/dp/B0186RUDTQ?crid=12A6YTAZGMHB5&keywords=six+moon+designs+umbrella&qid=1651271229&s=sporting-goods&sprefix=six+moon,sporting,140&sr=1-2&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=e08da15fd3b61fc0e09d94fe731b25c0&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)

- [Bear spray](http://www.avantlink.com/click.php?tt=cl&merchant_id=e295c418-295a-447c-b265-734e25f82503&website_id=80cf4755-ad50-4218-afb9-da253407b2ec&url=https://www.rei.com/product/154930/counter-assault-bear-deterrent-spray-81-fl-oz-2019&ctc=Backpacking%20Checklist) for grizzly country

- [Camera](https://www.amazon.com/Sony-DSC-RX100-Sensor-Digital-Camera/dp/B00889ST2G/ref=as_li_ss_tl?ie=UTF8&qid=1453697712&sr=8-1&keywords=sony+rx100&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=d92e6aa4a80de9acfc80f19ed06e85d6&language=en_US) + waterproof case/Ziploc

- Extra camera battery

- [Headlamp](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-hiking-backpacking-camping-headlamps/) (check batteries pre-trip)

- Extra batteries for long trips

- [Power bank](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-power-banks/) + charging cords

- [Wall plug](https://www.amazon.com/Charger-Adapter-Charging-Station-Replacement/dp/B07L1N7RG8?keywords=wall+plug+with+multiple+ports&qid=1651271378&sr=8-3&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=230f1849e8a975ded26382414a5313d9&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl) for thru-hikes

- Assorted [Ziploc bags](https://www.amazon.com/Ziploc-Variety-Pack-Freezer-Sandwich/dp/B01IPIL5JS?crid=3W0HRSFF9SA8Z&keywords=assorted+ziplock+bags+assorted+sizes&qid=1651271424&sprefix=assorted+ziploc,aps,143&sr=8-3&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=b9b12d80f8c1ea1452657b6e33cfa814&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)

- Cash, ID, credit card, insurance card

### EMERGENCY KIT

- [Whistle](https://www.amazon.com/LuxoGear-Emergency-Whistles-Lifeguard-Signaling/dp/B07RNNMZW3?crid=1IL3B30Q60FI&keywords=whistle+emergency&qid=1651271550&sprefix=whistle,aps,154&sr=8-1-spons&psc=1&spLa=ZW5jcnlwdGVkUXVhbGlmaWVyPUFMQ1g0Q0k5NUVJVzYmZW5jcnlwdGVkSWQ9QTA3MzUxMTExTFpMUDc0R1QwVE1DJmVuY3J5cHRlZEFkSWQ9QTAxMjQ3NTI5OTdERFNYM1RSR0smd2lkZ2V0TmFtZT1zcF9hdGYmYWN0aW9uPWNsaWNrUmVkaXJlY3QmZG9Ob3RMb2dDbGljaz10cnVl&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=8627d36d5c0e127dd9a516311ee5fa9a&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)

## Backpacking Tips

**LIGHTEN YOUR LOAD** – Start by weeding out things you don’t need. Be careful with every choice you make, a few ounces here and there can add a lot of weight in the end. A lightweight backpacking checklist, like the one here, will help you to focus on essential items. Next, focus on lightening your heaviest gear: shelter, backpack, and sleeping bag. Switching your traditional big three out for lightweight options is the best opportunity for weight savings, especially when you’re starting out. If you invest in a lightweight shelter, backpack, and sleeping bag, you can easily cut 10 or more pounds and be well on your way to having an ultralight backpacking setup.

**CLOTHING FOR BACKPACKING** – The [clothing you pack](https://www.cleverhiker.com/hiking/backpacking-amp-hiking-clothing-101-tips-for-creating-the-perfect-ultralight-clothing-system/) will change slightly depending on the conditions you expect to encounter on specific trips, but the fundamentals remain the same. Clothing made with quick-drying fabrics that wick moisture away from your skin are best to help your body thermoregulate and stay comfortable in both hot and cold environments. Nylon, polyester, wool, bamboo, silk, and synthetic blends are all good options. Avoid cotton – it absorbs moisture and takes a long time to dry, which can cause a variety of problems including blisters and chafing. Choose items that can be worn together in layers. [Fleece](https://www.cleverhiker.com/apparel/best-fleece-jackets/) and [goose-down](https://www.cleverhiker.com/apparel/best-down-jackets/) have the best warmth-to-weight ratio and make the best insulation materials for backpackers. Rain gear should be lightweight, breathable, and waterproof.

**BACKPACKING FOOD** – Good food is really important for any backpacking trip, so it’s well worth the effort to put together a simple meal plan before your trip. Keeping food weight down is a critical backpacking skill that usually takes experience to master. A good place to start is our [Guide to Lightweight Backpacking Food](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/lightweight-backpacking-food-guide-meal-planning-nutrition/). Most seasoned backpackers opt for lightweight, calorically-dense foods that are very easy to prepare. Packaged [freeze-dried meals](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-freeze-dried-meals/) and [snack foods](https://www.cleverhiker.com/hiking/best-energy-bars/) can be great, but keep in mind, they tend to be very high in sodium/sugar, which can take their toll, if eaten in excess.

Another approach is to [prepare your own backpacking meals](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/13-great-backpacking-meal-recipes-amp-food-dehydration-tips/), using a [food dehydrator](https://www.amazon.com/Nesco-FD-75A-Snackmaster-Dehydrator-White/dp/B0090WOCN0/ref=as_li_ss_tl?ie=UTF8&qid=1516468553&sr=8-3&keywords=food+dehydrator&linkCode=sl1&tag=trx-clever00793-20&linkId=1ccf36dcfb4c512ac6c09ad7a228b963) to dry meats, fruits, veggies, and sauces. Combining them with spices and quick-cooking or easily rehydrated dried goods such as pasta, couscous, instant potatoes, instant refried beans, and minute rice is a great way to customize your own highly-nutritious meals. This method takes more time and effort, and you must be more willing to carry more weight, but making your meals can be more cost-effective and healthier for long trips. Our approach is usually a mix of both methods. For more specifics about food, check out our [Best Lightweight Backpacking Food guide](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/lightweight-backpacking-food-guide-meal-planning-nutrition/), where we outline our general backpacking food strategy and suggest some of [our favorite meals](https://www.cleverhiker.com/backpacking/best-freeze-dried-meals/).
